newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Buying mood raises Bucharest share prices.
newsitem.headline: Buying mood raises Bucharest share prices.

text.p: A rush for Bucharest first-tier stocks extended from last week pushed up the prices of two of the four listings on Tuesday, helping the tier account for more than 90 percent of turnover.
Two independent indices, on the rise for more sessions in a row, touched new year highs.

Heavier demand than supply sent up most of the stocks on the second tier, where trading was otherwise dull. Eight companies had no deals and seven were suspended pending announcements on last year's results.

"Besides demand outrunning offers, prices rose today as an effect of the special trade last week," said a broker. "Investors were buying heavily as if to try to prevent the purchase of a bigger package in a special trade."

Last week, high-cap Azomures fertiliser maker had a special deal -- a large trade outside the market reported to the exchange later -- worth more than 20 billion lei. The deal sent turnover to a record high of 25.73 billion lei.
Traders said they expected the bull run for first-tier stocks to continue on Wednesday, when they predicted turnover would be around 5.0 billion lei.
On the first tier, pharmaceuticals Antibiotice and Terapia gained 350 and 300 lei respectively, closing at 4,650 and 4,100.

Selling pressure towards the end of the trading day depressed the prices of high-caps Azomures and Oltchim chemical plant. Azomures closed 800 lei lower at 1,700 and Oltchim lost 280 lei to close at 1,410.
Acceptable price variation on the bourse is plus/minus 50 percent.
On the second tier, the bright spot was Policolor dye maker, which had around 300 million lei in turnover and closed 125 lei stronger at 2,525.
The VAB and the BIG unofficial indices rose by 8.0 and 10.27 percent respectively from the previous session. The BIG first-tier index jumped by 13.16 percent to 2,461.67 points.
